newsitem.title: UK: Reinsurance market to stay competitive - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Reinsurance market to stay competitive - S&P.

text.p: Globalisation, shareholder demands and a soft market are all adding to the competitive pressures on reinsurance companies, ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Thursday.

"Pressure is placed on the reinsurer to not only maintain a conservative capital level to meet the potential needs of the policyholder but also achieve acceptable returns on equity," S&P said in its 'Top 100 Reinsurers Ratings List'.
"This pressure is further exacerbated by the soft pricing in the market with no real indication that the underlying risk exposures have been mitigated," it added.
The insurance market as a whole has seen premium rates decline in the last three or four years from cyclical peaks.

Analysts and industry players expect this downward trend to continue as long as claims experience follows the pattern of recent years, when the size and number of insured losses has been at or below historical levels on a global scale.
However, there will be opportunities, as well as challenges, for companies which react aggressively to the intense competition, the ratings agency said.

On the profit front, the industry should roughly break even at the underwriting level for 1996. The combined ratio -- claims and costs as a percentage of premium income should be around 100 percent -- S&P said.
The outlook for 1997 is less favourable as the gradual decline in rates in recent years is likely to impact on profitably.
S&P also forecasts a change in the ratings landscape for reinsurers, with a more balanced mix of downgrades and upgrades.

Ratings upgrades have far outnumbered downgrades in the last two years, in large part because of industry consolidation, which has "tended to enhance the security of those companies being acquired without straining the financial resources of the acquirers".
Pressure on ratings will come from a combination of the need to provide security for policyholders at the same time as market conditions are deteriorating, S&P said.
